review_text_raw:
Great idea, but bad execution. A for effort but C on the result.

PROS:
- Technical polish. The UI looks good and the videos, picture and audio are of good quality.
- The developers did seem to put their heart into this. It is not easy to make games involving so much detail, actors and voice work
- Interesting concept. While not original, piercing the story together through different apps on the phone was neat
- Some puzzles were neat like finding a phone number hidden in Twitter posts or creating a specific Tinder profile, because they fit the concept of the game really well

CONS:
- All the characters are downright unlikable.. I didn't care for Anna one bit and if there was an ending to kill them all off I would have took it. And when I mean all, I really mean all. Every single one, including her mother and the HR lady. I guess only the cat gets a pass and even then I'm not sure
- Unrealistic voice work. Most characters speak very unnaturally. The biggest offender being Greg who talks like he is in a kid's anime
- You can only speak to people when they are online, but they always pop up immediately when you need them to make progress, making it very obvious you are playing a videogame. A few seconds delay would have done wonders for the immersion
- Repetitive gameplay. Most of the time you will be doing the same "construct a phrase" or "remake a picture" puzzle and the whole cycle of restoring the phone data should have only happened once.
- Cheap cheap "horror" with zero atmosphere but instead lots of dumb jump-scares (really really a lot) and in-your-face weirdness. No subtlety whatsoever, making the "horror" cheap, pointless and braindead
- The ending. I felt dumber after the villain reveal and finished the game. Not sure I can put up with another run to see the other endings. I was expecting something stupid, but this worse than I expected

They really should have either cut the "horror" and gone full psychological crime thriller (which would have worked really well with the gameplay) or just go full ham and make the weirdness go on through the whole experience escalating more and more.
Instead you get a detective story ruined by awful jump scares or a horror story bogged down by boring detectice work. I would prefer the former as the later was really really bad, inspired by the worst horror movies the '10s had to offer.

I can forgive the bad dialogues and bad acting due to being an indie game, but I would suggest the developers to at least not use outdated memes in people's speech.

Only buy it on sale and expect a mediocre experience that pisses you off because it had the potential to be much better.

review_text_raw:
Playable, but not to my tastes.

Simulacra is a simple investigative game that requires patience not for the investigation itself, but for its unnatural writing (very clearly non-native English) and its amateurish acted scenes. Jokes dropped like lead balloons, tension dissipated, and what should have been an exciting climax was simply uncomfortable.

The puzzles themselves were relatively entertaining - flicking between apps to piece together information - but the game's "OS" seemed almost incapable of multitasking, and switching between tabs would typically lose form entry data, making the process far more tedious than it should have been.

The game encourages the player to play through multiple times (with a fast-dialogue option after completion), but one playthrough felt like a slog, so I'm unlikely to sit through it again. If you happen to have it in your Steam library, give it a shot, but don't get your hopes too high.

review_text_raw:
Basically "Black Mirror: The Game," which can be a good thing if that's what you're into. It's an interesting premise and I respect them for trying something different, but they fall into the same trap that Black Mirror does: saying "technology is bad!" and hammering that idea home over and over and over for hours gets boring after a while.

Within the first ten minutes, the game does a good job establishing the theme of "Technology connects us but leaves us feeling alone." The problem is that once it does that, it doesn't really know where to go from there. There's no meditation on what we as a society can do to work on this, or explorations of how one can learn to find self-worth in such a shallow world. It's just a repeating loop of talking to online dating matches (all losers and jerks), going through Anna's browsing history (all online shopping and personality quizzes), and texting her ex-bf, who's verbally abusive and cheated on her when they were dating. We get an occasional break when we go through her emails, where we learn that she keeps getting rejected from vet school, her boss is unappreciative, and her co-worker is constantly harassing her.

It's all so...bleak, which is fine, but there's just no point to any of it. Like, okay, I get it, the internet sucks and is making us all act like terrible people, but *what's your point*? Should we do something about it? Or just accept it? 

The gameplay is engaging but not very complex, meaning this game relies on its story, which just didn't have enough depth for me. Maybe it's my own fault for being more optimistic about the state of the world, idk, I was just hoping for a story with something more to say other than "phones bad, am i right?"

Every attempt at being scary, disturbing, or creepy just came off as obnoxious. Every single sound is loud and abrasive to the point of being painfully annoying. Please stop making people send so many messages with individual words per notification while I'm trying to read something else. 

The writing is realistic in some areas but feels like a hypercorrection in others. Not every sentence needs a typo. The rest feels out of place. I'm all for cheesy FMVs having loved Harvester but this felt overacted in a bad way. Greg sounded like an American anime dub. 

Love the concept. Would like to see the same type of game done better with more investigative work required to complete and not just simple repetitive word/picture puzzles. I'll probably even try the second in the hope that it makes those improvements.

review_text_raw:
Got this via Humble ... but I gotta say, ugh, phff, well, no.

Maybe someone can find this interesting, but to me I just played it out of curiosity to see what it's about. And it only took 3 hours for 1 playthrough.

Gameplay is minimal. You "chat" with people mostly and sometimes you gotta play a bit of detective, but, nah.

I guess it might have been more interesting if the story had actually been good, if the characters had been likeable, but they're all very annoying people, even Ashley. Seriously, this game does not have a single human being ... or maybe it IS close to real and that would be even more depressing.

Using the apps was tedious, switching between apps meant progress was mostly lost, which slows down progress. Some hints are so "obscure" that you will have forgotten all about them when you actually need them halfway through the game. Some things are illogical.

The dialogue could carry such a game, but it's not well-written (and they do not speak EN as their mother tongue). It's cringy, annoying, irritating, endless (seriously, just write out the text in 1 message, not 10).

In any case the story makes little sense. Spoiler: It's not a thriller, it's "supernatural". That is made clear from the very beginning, but not on the store page. I expected an actual crime, not some pseudo horror trip with bad "explanations".

Honestly, I just wanted to tell the guys to leave me the fuck alone. I'll try out the 2nd game as well to see what they changed, but I do hope there's a "fuck you all" button.

review_text_raw:
Incredibly disappointing. Started out with a lot of promise, but quickly dove into a linear, absolutely silly plot that doesn't deserve a second play-through. Nothing you do actually matters except for the bearing it has on the last conversation of the game. Wish you could change one response? Too bad, restart the entire game. Excited to experience a different ending? Do EXACTLY the same thing for 3 straight hours but make one different decision to get a different ending.

Text has so many misspellings I couldn't keep track. Voice-overs are rare but still manage to not match the text on screen or mispronounce words completely. Lazy effort all around.

There is so much that could have gone right with this game, but it ended up being a mediocre visual novel with a nonsensical plot, very little character development, and an overall feeling of "wow, what a waste of time."

I found the game interesting and would have loved to see it through,but i couldn't bring myself to finish it.

In other reviews it's mention that it might be a bit of a slog to get through,but i found the information gathering,while repetitive to be quite nice and clever.

What stops me if the sudden jumpscars,they are not telegraphed well (there is very little to no indication that a jumpscared will happen,no tension build up,none of that,one moment you are looking through apps and suddenly you're struck with a jumpsacre when returning to the homepage).

As someone who is quite sensitive to jumpscares,even already knowing about the fact that there were jumpscares,the first major one was what stopped me from wanting to play.If the jumpscares were more subtle and less horrific i think it would have been more possible for me to finish,or at least get further in.

Another issue i had was that the game had no way of changing the volume inside the game,and i had to change it manually on my computer,someone who is less technically literate would probably have gotten an unintended jumpscare from the sudden volume from purely opening the game

The voice acting (with greg specifically) any many dialog was unrealistic,but i foudn it to be a more enjoyable part of the game,as they contrasted the poorly executed jumpscares in levity,though i would understand if it was not the intended effect.

it is truly a shame,because using the mediums and technology for this kind of horror would have been truly wonderful,clever and thought provoking,and even if nihilistic,the story  (as far as i have heard in other's videos and such) and how it applies it's title to it's themes could have been great.

i might look into it's sequals,but i may simply not have the stomach to actually go through on playing them,i hope you have a lovely day :D
